summary: Verified env-driven admin password re-sync (seed_admin) that underlies the deployment login fix. Baseline login, temporary password swap + restart, restore, brute-force resilience, and deploy static checks all pass. System restored to Broadcast2026!.

test_results.baseline_login: PASS - POST /api/auth/login returns 200 with role=admin; GET /api/auth/me with Bearer returns admin user
test_results.env_resync_new_password: PASS - After setting ADMIN_PASSWORD=TmpPass_9f3k and restarting backend, login with TmpPass_9f3k -> 200
test_results.env_resync_old_password_rejected: PASS - After resync, login with old Broadcast2026! -> 401 (Invalid email or password)
test_results.restore: PASS - Reset ADMIN_PASSWORD to Broadcast2026!, restart, login -> 200 role=admin
test_results.brute_force_not_permanent: PASS - 3 wrong attempts followed by correct password -> 200 (lockout is per-identifier and temporary, MAX_ATTEMPTS=5)
test_results.docker_compose_check: PASS - deploy/docker-compose.yml is valid YAML; backend service environment interpolates ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET, DB_NAME, CORS_ORIGINS from ${...}

critical_code_review_comments: seed_admin in /app/backend/auth.py correctly updates existing admin password_hash when env password does not verify against stored hash — this is exactly the mechanism that makes the installer-generated ADMIN_PASSWORD authoritative on user servers.

docker-compose sets CORS_ORIGINS default to '*' which combined with credentialed cookies (samesite=none, secure) may be problematic in browsers; consider requiring explicit origins in production. Not blocking for this task.
context_for_next_testing_agent: ADMIN_PASSWORD is restored to Broadcast2026! in /app/backend/.env and backend restarted. seed_admin re-syncs the admin password on every startup from env, so any change to ADMIN_PASSWORD is picked up after `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`.
rca of the issue: In the user's on-server deployment, a baked backend/.env (with the demo password) was overriding the installer-generated ADMIN_PASSWORD injected by docker-compose environment. Fixed by (1) /app/.dockerignore excluding backend/.env from the image, and (2) deploy/docker-compose.yml explicitly interpolating ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD/JWT_SECRET/DB_NAME/CORS_ORIGINS via ${...}, making the container env authoritative. seed_admin then re-syncs the admin password_hash on startup to whatever ADMIN_PASSWORD is set to. Verified end-to-end in preview.
